strings.d1.s0.name: Zinciriye Medresesi
strings.d1.s0.tips: Mardin's highest madrasa; from the domed terrace you look over the Mesopotamian plain. Cool in the morning.
strings.d1.s1.name: Mardin Grand Mosque
strings.d1.s1.tips: Artuqid minaret in the middle of the bazaar.
strings.d1.s2.name: Mardin Coppersmiths' Bazaar
strings.d1.s2.tips: Copper, almond candy and Mardin soap; donkeys still carry goods along the stone lanes.
strings.d1.s3.name: Cercis Murat Konağı
strings.d1.s3.tips: Syriac-Mardin cuisine in a stone mansion; order the stuffed ribs (kaburga dolması) in advance. Terrace views.
strings.d1.s4.name: Kasimiye Madrasa
strings.d1.s4.tips: Twin-domed madrasa with a courtyard pool; the plain turns red at sunset.
strings.d1.b0.name: Seyr-i Merdin Kafe
strings.d1.b0.tips: Terrace café for coffee and Mardin pastry (Mardin çöreği).
strings.d1.b1.name: Mardin Museum
strings.d1.b1.tips: Archaeology museum in the former patriarchate; an indoor option instead of the madrasa.
strings.d2.s0.name: Deyrulzafaran Monastery
strings.d2.s0.tips: 1,500-year-old Syriac monastery; guided tour covers the sun temple and patriarch tombs. Take the first group in the morning.
strings.d2.s1.name: Kırklar Church
strings.d2.s1.tips: Active Syriac church in Old Mardin; quiet courtyard.
strings.d2.s2.name: Antik Mardin Sofrası
strings.d2.s2.tips: Ikbebet, sembusek and dobo in a mansion restaurant.
strings.d2.s3.name: Şahkulubey Mansion
strings.d2.s3.tips: Stone mansion and courtyard; walk on through the bazaar lanes.
strings.d2.s4.name: Mardin Castle Viewpoint
strings.d2.s4.tips: The castle is military, but the viewpoint at its foot is open; city and plain at sunset.
strings.d2.b0.name: Mardin Kebapçısı Yusuf Usta
strings.d2.b0.tips: Mardin kebab and içli köfte (stuffed bulgur meatballs).
strings.d2.b1.name: Sakıp Sabancı Mardin City Museum
strings.d3.s0.name: Dara Ancient City
strings.d3.s0.tips: 30 km from Mardin; Roman cistern, necropolis and rock tombs, known as the "Ephesus of Mesopotamia".
strings.d3.s1.name: Dara Village Breakfast
strings.d3.s1.tips: Mardin breakfast in a village house; crumbled cheese and bulgur with eggs.
strings.d3.s2.name: Savur
strings.d3.s2.tips: Stone town nicknamed Little Mardin; castle, mansions and mulberry orchards.
strings.d3.s3.name: Savur Kahveci Konağı
strings.d3.s3.tips: Mırra (bitter coffee) and mulberry molasses in a mansion.
strings.d3.b0.name: Kızıltepe Grand Mosque
strings.d3.b0.tips: Artuqid mosque; an alternative to Savur.
strings.d3.b1.name: Dara Kahve Evi
strings.d4.s0.name: Midyat Konukevi
strings.d4.s0.tips: The mansion from the TV series Sıla; terrace and stonework. Midyat is 1 hour away.
strings.d4.s1.name: Midyat Old Bazaar
strings.d4.s1.tips: Telkari (silver filigree) masters and Syriac wine.
strings.d4.s2.name: Mor Barsavmo Church
strings.d4.s3.name: Midyat Kasr-ı Nehroz Restaurant
strings.d4.s3.tips: Syriac cuisine in a stone mansion; try perde pilavı (pastry-wrapped rice) and alluciye.
strings.d4.s4.name: Mor Gabriel Monastery
strings.d4.s4.tips: One of the world's oldest active monasteries (397); guided tour, mosaics. 20 km from Midyat.
strings.d4.b0.name: Midyat Gelüşke Hanı
strings.d4.b1.name: Hasankeyf
strings.d4.b1.tips: New Hasankeyf and the castle; an alternative to Mor Gabriel (1 hour).
strings.d5.s0.name: Mor Yakup Church Nusaybin
strings.d5.s0.tips: 4th-century church and the excavation of the School of Nisibis; on the Syrian border.
strings.d5.s1.name: Nusaybin Zeynel Abidin Mosque
strings.d5.s1.tips: Tomb and mosque, next to the church.
strings.d5.s2.name: Nusaybin Çarşı Lokantası
strings.d5.s2.tips: Town eatery serving ribs and pilaf.
strings.d5.s3.name: Girnavaz Mound
strings.d5.s3.tips: Assyrian mound near Nusaybin; excavation site.
strings.d5.b0.name: Nusaybin Kahvaltıcısı
strings.d5.b1.name: Mardin Dara Road Viewpoint
strings.d5.b1.tips: Views over the plain; an alternative to the mound.
strings.d6.s0.name: Mardin Soap Workshop
strings.d6.s0.tips: See how terebinth (bıttım) soap is made, and shop.
strings.d6.s1.name: Mardin Protestant Church
strings.d6.s1.tips: Restored church, now a cultural centre.
strings.d6.s2.name: Mardin Abbaras
strings.d6.s2.tips: Vaulted lanes running beneath houses; cool passages.
strings.d6.s3.name: Mardin Leyli Kahvaltı
strings.d6.s3.tips: Mardin breakfast with clotted cream and honey, plus sembusek.
strings.d6.s4.name: Şehidiye Madrasa
strings.d6.s4.tips: Madrasa with a minaret and a tea garden; sunset.
strings.d6.b0.name: Mardin Mırra Evi
strings.d6.b1.name: Latifiye Mosque
strings.d6.b1.tips: Artuqid mosque; an alternative to Şehidiye.
strings.d7.s0.name: Mardin Badem Şekercisi
strings.d7.s0.tips: Almond candy, Mardin soap and telkari souvenirs.
strings.d7.s1.name: Mardin 1. Cadde
strings.d7.s1.tips: Old Mardin's main street; one last walk.
strings.d7.s2.name: Mardin Kahvaltı Konağı
strings.d7.b0.name: Mardin Maristan Kafe
strings.d7.b0.tips: Café in an old Artuqid hospital; mırra and a terrace.
strings.d7.b1.name: Emir Hamamı Mardin
strings.note0: Mardin Airport is 20 minutes from the city. A car is useless in Old Mardin, so walk. For Midyat, Dara and Nusaybin, use a car or minibus.
strings.note1: Order the stuffed ribs (kaburga dolması) in advance at Cercis Murat. Mırra is a bitter coffee, and the cup is handed back. Almond candy and terebinth soap make good souvenirs.
strings.note2: Summer temperatures top 40°C: sightsee from 08:30 to 12:00 and after 17:00, rest in mansion courtyards at midday, and carry 3 litres of water.
strings.note3: Respect service times at Syriac churches and monasteries. Deyrulzafaran is by guided tour only, and short sleeves are not allowed.
strings.note4: The streets of Old Mardin are steep and paved with stone; wear comfortable shoes and cool off in the abbaras.
strings.note5: Sunset at Kasimiye is Mardin's most famous moment; arrive 1 hour early.
